definition: Self-view is the way a person sees and relates to themselves. In this source, it refers especially to a self-attitude that can become more positive and mindful through meditation or mindfulness practice.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence (“Self-view is the way a person sees and relates to themselves”) is a general characterization that is not explicitly stated in the provided packet.

The packet discusses “mindfulness-enlightened self-view and attitude” and positive changes in attitudes toward the self resulting from mindfulness/meditation, but it does not directly support the broader general definition of “self-view” given in the first sentence.
Because the first substantive claim is unsupported, the definition cannot be accepted as supported by the packet.
The packet supports “self-view” as part of a “mindful self” and as a self-attitude, but it does not support the broader gloss that it is “the way a person sees and relates to themselves.”

The packet says mindfulness practices can be associated with positive changes in self-attitude, but it does not support the stronger phrasing that self-view “can become more positive and mindful” in general.
